newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar dives vs yen in Tokyo on upbeat BOJ survey.
newsitem.headline: Dollar dives vs yen in Tokyo on upbeat BOJ survey.

text.p: 0622 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar dived against the yen in Tokyo on Wednesday, sent staggering by a strong improvement in business sentiment shown in the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey. It briefly sank by as much as one and a half yen.
Traders who had anticipated weak figures in the survey were caught off guard and falls in yen bond prices and gains in stocks prompted overseas operators to buy the yen.

"The figure was out of line with the previous market expectations," said Kazuhiko Endo, a manager of the finance department at Marubeni Corp. "Since the dollar strayed out of a 114-115 yen range, selling pressure could intensify."
The diffusion index for manufacturers, a key gauge of business confidence, rose to plus seven in June from plus two in March, when the previous survey was conducted.
Economists' forecasts for the major manufacturers index had ranged from minus four to plus four.
The data rekindled expectations of a rise in Japan's official discount rate sometime in the latter part of the year.
"Overseas operators are particularly sensitive to Japan's interest rates, and the dollar may be sold further in overseas trade later today," said Marubeni's Endo.
The yield of the key 182nd JGB was at 2.495 percent at 0651 GMT, up 0.155 percent from Tuesday's close, and the 225-share Nikkei average rose 337.34 points to end at 20,679.27.
"Since yen bond and euroyen futures prices fell and stocks gained after the tankan results, overseas operators coolly bought the yen for the dollar," said a Japanese bank dealer.
Meanwhile, dollar buying by Japanese importers and investors supported it at around 113.30 yen, he added.
Many dealers said the dollar could come under selling pressure as the BOJ survey showed that the economic recovery was driven not by domestic demand but by exports.

A BOJ official told reporters that one big factor behind the improvement in manufacturers' sentiment was a rise in exports. This will not please Washington, which has reiterated warnings against a rise in Japan's trade surplus.

"Given strong figures in the manufacturing sector, there is a great possibility that the trade issue will become a topic in the currency market," said Hiroyuki Hashiguchi, a dealer at international finance department at Hitachi Ltd.
Hashiguchi said the dollar could head towards 110-105 yen, while its recovery to 115 yen be capped by selling by investors and exporters.

A dealer at a U.S. bank in Singapore said: "I tend to favour the downside (for the dollar) but it may not go immediately." He added: "The 113 figure is pretty important and I think it will go fairly soon."
Traders in Tokyo also said they were wary of selling dollars aggressively below 113 yen because of the risk of talking up of the dollar by Japanese monetary authorities.
"I guess that the authorities will start talking up the dollar if it falls sharply below 113 yen," said a bank dealer.
A U.S. bank dealer said a decisive fall in the dollar to below 112.80 yen may pave the way for a dive below 112 yen.
The dollar closed at 114.90/95 yen and 1.7240/50 marks in New York on Tuesday.
